title: Intake guardrail + release embosser: deterministic metadata rollups and humanized changelog snippets
author: Clara Nguyen
description: Context and motivation: Our current model intake pipeline produces inconsistent metadata rollups and noisy release notes when multiple minor metadata edits happen across parallel commits. This causes downstream consumers (release digest, release inspector UI, and SDK onboarding docs) to show flickering or duplicate entries. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an intake guardrail that enforces a deterministic, idempotent metadata normalization and compacting step during model onboarding; and (2) a 'release embosser' service that synthesizes concise human-friendly changelog snippets from the compacted deltas, annotated with confidence tags and rollback hints. Implementation summary: - Intake guardrail: a new ingestion middleware (pkg/ingest/guardrail) that validates required fields, canonicalizes aliases (model_name/model_alias), collapses repeated key edits into a single canonical delta, and computes a stable fingerprint (sha256 hex) for the resulting metadata bundle. The guardrail runs both as a pre-commit hook for manual onboard flows and as a post-ingest transaction in the async intake worker. It emits structured validation warnings to telemetry and returns a stable 'ingest_id' to the caller. - Deterministic rollups: added deterministic delta-merging logic (pkg/registry/rollup) that merges multiple edits by ordering them by (timestamp, author_id, edit_type_priority) and applying a deterministic compositing function so the same set of edits always yields the same rollup. We also added compatibility heuristics for variant aliases and quantization hints. - Release embosser: a standalone small service (tools/release-embosser) that consumes rollup deltas and produces human-readable blurb candidates for release notes. Embosser outputs: short title (one line), 1-3 bullet summary lines, confidence level (high/medium/low), and an optional revert command for ops. The embosser includes templated examples for model performance profile changes, metadata-only edits, and variant promotions. - Tests and tooling: added unit tests for the normalization rules, property-based tests for the deterministic rollup function, a lightweight e2e harness that simulates concurrent onboard edits (tests/e2e/intake_race_test.go), and a Linters/CI addition to run the embosser smoke example during PR checks. Related work and docs: references ENG-4821 (intake stabilization epic) and design doc: /docs/designs/intake-guardrail.md. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag (intake.guardrail.enabled) and embosser.enabled; default OFF for 48 hours while monitoring telemetry. Migration notes: legacy metadata blobs are reprocessed via a backfill job (tools/backfill/compactify) — backfill included in this PR as a dry-run mode only. Single-line checklist: - [x] Add guardrail middleware and deterministic rollup - [x] Add release embosser service and templates - [x] Unit/property/e2e tests - [x] Feature flags, telemetry hooks, dry-run backfill - [x] Docs and developer guide entries (docs/onboard/guardrail.md)

release_notes:
- Added an intake guardrail that enforces canonicalized metadata, computes a stable ingest fingerprint, and reduces noisy rollup churn.
- Deterministic rollups ensure identical edit sets yield identical compacted metadata (reduces UI flicker and duplicate release entries).
- Release embosser produces concise, annotated changelog snippets (title, bullets, confidence, rollback hints) to populate release digests and SDK onboarding notes.
- Backfill dry-run included; ops-only gate required for real backfill.
- Feature flags: intake.guardrail.enabled, tools.embosser.enabled (default off).
notes_for_release_manager: This PR introduces backend behavior changes to onboarding. Keep feature flags off for the first 48 hours after deploy to monitor ingest/telemetry. Run backfill in dry-run and review preflight before enabling. Notify docs and SDK teams to expect more compact release snippets in the digest feed.
